steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Key movements: Bauhaus (form follows function, industrial production), Art Deco (geometric, luxurious), Memphis (playful, postmodern), De Stijl (abstract, primary colours).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Understanding design context helps you make informed choices — every design has cultural, social and technological influences.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Form follows function means the shape of an object should relate to its purpose — but this principle has been both followed and deliberately challenged.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your research should INFORM your own design decisions — understand WHY designers made their choices before adapting their approaches.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring designers and design movements. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with designers and design movements. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with designers and design movements. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to designers and design movements, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined o | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
